subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth exclude native device tokens and use only configured shared token/password/browser auth, or should it preserve native/operator token parity with the native app?
rationale: Both open draft PRs touch the same Dashboard auth surface but encode opposite credential policies, and merging either choice can change user auth behavior after upgrade.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Proceed with this PR's policy after rebasing it over current main, updating the endpoint-change path, and requiring macOS proof for shared token, password, and no-token browser prompt behavior.

options.title: Preserve native-token parity
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction if maintainers want the embedded Dashboard to receive native/operator tokens like the native connection.

options.title: Defer until a cross-platform native auth policy exists
options.body: Keep both branches paused while maintainers define how macOS, iOS, and Android native Control UI injection should treat stored device tokens versus shared secrets.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR's policy after rebasing it over current main, updating the endpoint-change path, and requiring macOS proof for shared token, password, and no-token browser prompt behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently updated the native macOS Dashboard paths that define the affected behavior.
